chapter_theme: The great saying 'that you are' (தத்துவமசி): its three words, 'you', 'that' and 'are', are placed in three turiyas, of the soul, of the Supreme and of Siva, and read by implication until the soul, its bonds and instruments left behind, becomes Siva. Tirumular calls this Vedanta's saying and Siddhanta's conclusion at once, and ends with the Lord's grace making the speaker spotless and every soul dancing as he makes it dance.
structure_note: 2568 to 2579 expound the saying through the turiyas, implication and the states; 2580 to 2582 turn to knowing, which the soul has only as Siva makes it know; 2583 to 2585 are the speaker's own experience of grace; 2586 closes on the Lord as the one who moves all.

2568.reading: The word 'you' is the soul in the soul's turiya, the word 'that' is in the supreme turiya to which it leaps, and the true word 'are' is in Siva's turiya; the truth of 'that you are' is that these fall away.
2568.nuance: தொம்பதம், தற்பதம் and அசிபதம் are the three words of tat tvam asi (tvam, tat, asi). சீவதுரியம், பரதுரியம் and சிவதுரியம் are the three turiyas of Tirumular's scheme. ஓவி விடும் (cease, fall away) is read as the three distinctions dissolving into one.

2569.reading: The soul beyond the thirty-six tattvas is the pure 'you'; 'that' is the end it reaches in the stilled state; when the soul that has gained this departs, in grace the glorious union of 'you', 'that' and 'are' is 'that you are'.
2569.nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is taken as the thirty-six tattvas and அணு as the soul. உபசாந்தம் and பிரசாதம் (grace) are technical stages; the order of the steps is compressed.

2570.reading: As in 'this is that Devadatta', the implication that both leaves and keeps applies; they call the stilled state 'you, that, are', and the soul so reached becomes the Supreme, Siva.
2570.nuance: அச்சோயம் தேவகத்தன் is read as sa ayam devadattah, the Vedantic example: the man seen now is the man seen before, so 'this' and 'that' keep the person and drop the time and place. The same mode is applied to 'that you are'. The reading of தேவகத்தன் as Devadatta is an inference.

2571.reading: 'You, that, are' becoming one is the 'that you are' of Vedanta, reached by tapas; it is Siva, and that is Siddhanta-Vedanta.
2571.nuance: The last line joins சித்தாந்தம் and வேதாந்தம் into one word, a claim that the two conclusions meet. Line 2 (அவைமன்னா வந்து வயத்தேகமான) is obscure; the reading of துவந்தத்தசி and தொந்தத்தசி as forms of 'you-that-are' is the usual one.

2572.reading: They call the wordless void in which turiya subsides the rare Supreme, and do not deny it form; but who knows the rare ground where the one, the highest of the high, arises?
2572.nuance: பாழ் (void, waste) for the highest state is a recurring term in Tirumular. ஆகாரி தன்று என்னார் may mean 'they do not say it is formless' or the reverse; the verse may be correcting those who stop at the void.

2573.reading: If one seeks the words 'you', 'that' and 'are' above the three trusted turiyas, that state becomes the state where soul and Supreme can be called Siva, the true thing.
2573.nuance: முத்துரியம் recalls the three turiyas of 2568. உம்பதம் உம்பதம் ஆகும் is obscure; it may mean 'that state becomes your state'.

2574.reading: In the turiya so placed, in the bliss of one's own form, he took the teaching of Om he had received, released it in the true heart, and stood having reached true awareness just as it was given.
2574.nuance: சொரூபானந்தம் (bliss of one's own form) and பிரணவ உபதேசம் (the teaching of Om) are technical; who 'he' is, the disciple or the Lord, is not stated.

2575.reading: Place the five states beginning with waking in nada and the rest, put the corpse-like mala behind, and then seek the king who is beyond mind and speech, the pure Siva-state of being and peace.
2575.nuance: நனவாதி ஐந்து are waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and the beyond. பிணமா மலம் (mala like a corpse) is taken as anava, inert and binding. சத்தாதி சாந்தி may be a list of states (being, and the rest, peace) rather than one phrase.

2576.reading: It is not filled up, since nothing is outside it; it takes no name, since no speech reaches it; it joins nothing, since there is nothing else; without any cause it shows itself, such is its nature.
2576.nuance: The verse is built as three negations each with its reason (இலாமையின்), then a positive. பூரணியாது and பேரணியாது are uncertain forms; 'not filled' and 'not named' are guesses from the reasons given.

2577.reading: The great saying that stood as 'you are that', once it ripens into 'I have become that', is the great grace of glorious Nandi that makes one Siva; then bliss itself becomes Nandi.
2577.nuance: The verse turns the second-person saying (நீ அது ஆனாய்) into a first-person realization (அது நான் ஆனேன்) and credits the change to Nandi's grace, not to understanding alone. The last line is uncertain: அனந்தான் may be ஆனந்தம் or அனந்தன் (the endless).

2578.reading: The soul becoming the Supreme, the high supreme soul becoming rare Siva, as the Siva-Veda calls him the highest of the high, is the form of Om beyond any fitting word.
2578.nuance: இரியிலும் in line 3 is obscure. ஓமயம் is taken as 'made of Om'; it may also be read as 'Om-pervaded'.

2579.reading: Mouth, nose, the crown of the head and the top: they stand as the first places; nadi and the rest, speech and the rest, sakala and the rest, and the far-reaching light are the five Siva-states.
2579.nuance: The verse lists places in the head and categories (நாடி, வாக்கு, சகலம்) in the compressed manner of the yogic chapters; the five Siva-states (சிவகதி ஐந்து) are not named, and I can't fix how the lists map onto each other.

2580.reading: Those who do not know the sign of putting away both knowing and not-knowing, and tending as Lord, without knowing separation, the Siva who stands everywhere as dense knowledge, cannot grasp him.
2580.nuance: அறிவு அறியாமை இரண்டும் அகற்றி: both the soul's limited knowledge and its ignorance are to be set aside, since Siva is செறிவு அறிவு, knowledge itself. பிறிவு அறியாது (not knowing separation) is the condition of worship here. Sengalvaraya marks a parallel for line 1.

2581.reading: The knowers know water and fire, and know water and its mixing; but unless the Knower who is there makes us know, we do not know the knowledge the Knower knows.
2581.nuance: The repeated அறிவு makes the point by sound: the soul can know the elements, but knowledge of the Lord comes only as he makes it known (அறிவிக்கின்). This is the Siddhanta claim that the soul knows only with the Lord's help, as tradition takes it. அப்புங் கலப்பும் is unclear.

2582.reading: Nandi is within the beyond-state and yet transcends it; the soul within the beyond-state is without knowledge; the abiding soul that gains understanding and leaves its rolling becomes one, the supreme soul settling into the Lord.
2582.nuance: அதீதம் is the state beyond turiya. The contrast is between the Lord, who is in it and beyond it, and the soul, which in it is knowledgeless until it gains மதி. உருள் (rolling) is taken as the round of births. பதியிற் பதியும் plays on பதி as Lord and as 'settle'.

2583.reading: As the gods stood before him to worship his feet, the Lord stood before me in grace so that I could worship his crown, and the brow-eyed one said: see now all that you once imagined in worship on earth.
2583.nuance: The contrast of feet for the gods and crown for the speaker is a reading; பண்டு பாவித்தது (what you imagined before) suggests that earlier worship in imagination is now fulfilled in sight. கடிதொழ காணன்னும் is obscure.

2584.reading: The spotless one with a spotless body, the unborn, came into my heart and said 'this one is my servant'; the gold-bodied one whom the gods praise could take away my impurity, saying 'be spotless'.
2584.nuance: நின்மலம் opens the verse and returns in the Lord's command, so the Lord's purity becomes the speaker's. The Lord claims the speaker as his servant (அடியான்) before he cleanses him.

2585.reading: Renouncing, I entered and saw the light that holds the flame; my heart flew up and lay prostrate, and the king of the heavens, whom I had never forgotten, set me here so that I would not die and be born again.
2585.nuance: பறந்தது என் உள்ளம் பணிந்து கிடந்தே joins rapture and surrender in one line. இறந்து பிறவாமல் ஈங்கு வைத்தான் places release here, in this life, which suits the chapter's claim that the soul becomes Siva.

2586.reading: Body, mouth, eyes, nose and ears, the inner instruments and all else: since every soul dances as the Lord makes it dance, the fullness without hands or mouth is seen everywhere as truth.
2586.nuance: இறை ஆட்ட ஆடலால் (dancing as the Lord makes it dance) makes all the soul's action his. Sengalvaraya notes the parallel in Appar's Thevaram, ஆட்டுவித்தால் ஆரொருவர் ஆடாதாரே. கைவாயிலா நிறை (fullness with no hands or mouth) is the Lord who acts through all without organs of his own.

links.note: 2568 sets out the saying analytically, word by word and turiya by turiya; 2577 says what completes it: 'you are that' must become 'I have become that', and this happens by Nandi's grace.

2580 tells the seeker to put away both knowing and not-knowing before Siva who is knowledge itself; 2581 gives the reason: the soul knows the elements, but knows the Lord only as the Lord makes it know.

source_issues: 2580: line 1 reads அகற்றிப் செறிவு, a misprint for அகற்றிச் செறிவு.
2586: line 2 reads அகில்மும், probably for அகிலமும், and line 3 எவ்வா யியுரும், which Sengalvaraya's citation gives as எவ்வா யுயிரும்.
2568: line 4 is printed மோவி விடும், probably ஓவி விடும் run on from the previous word.
2571 line 2 (அவைமன்னா வந்து வயத்தேகமான), 2578 line 3 (இரியிலும்) and 2583 line 4 (கடிதொழ காணன்னும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
